# Setting Up a Fuji JobMaker Print Controller

OrderHub Desktop (OHD) sends jobs to a Fujifilm Frontier through **JobMaker**, the order hot folder that the Fuji software watches. For each job, OHD copies the images into a folder the Fuji PC can read. It then writes a small order file (`.txt`) into the JobMaker hot folder, telling Frontier which images to print, at which size and on which paper surface.

This article covers:

- adding a Fuji JobMaker controller;
- what every setting does;
- telling OHD which print code and surface each product uses (**Channel Mappings**);
- combining jobs from the same order.

![Fuji Jobmaker Jobcard](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/749516b0-849a-446d-b67e-b666e9e7761d.png)

---

## Before You Start

* JobMaker must already be set up on the Fuji PC, with a hot folder the OHD computer can write to.
* You'll need a folder for the images that both the OHD computer and the Fuji PC can reach, for example a shared folder on your server.
* You'll need your Frontier's **Quick Print** codes (for example **6x4** or **5x7**) and paper **surface** names (for example **Lustre** or **Glossy**), exactly as they're set up on the Fuji side.

---

## Adding the Controller

1. In OHD, go to **Settings → Routing**.
2. In the **Order Controllers** section, click **+ Add Controller**. The **Add Controller** window opens.
3. In **Name**, type a name you'll recognise, for example **Fuji Frontier**.
4. In **Type**, choose **Fuji JobMaker**.
   * Note: a new controller opens as **Noritsu (DPOF)**, so always change the **Type** first.
5. Next to **Image Staging Root**, click **Browse...** and choose the folder for the images.
6. In **Image Path (Fuji JobMaker view)**, type the same folder the way the Fuji PC reaches it.
7. Fill in **Printer Name**, **Auto Correct**, **Back Print Mode** and **Failure Timeout** (explained below).

![Image Paths](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/41434d64-75ca-4463-8b0b-e444f34044f7.png)

### Setting the Output Path

The **Output Path** is further down the same window, below **Failure Timeout**, so scroll down to find it.

8. Next to **Output Path**, click **Browse...** and choose the JobMaker hot folder.
9. Set **Auto Print** and **Combine jobs from the same order** (explained below).
10. Click **Save Controller**.

![Fuji Output Paths](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/4111f003-68b3-4e32-84ae-6b95af3245b6.png)

Once saved, the controller appears as a card in **Order Controllers**, with **Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Delete** buttons and an **Auto Print** tick box.

* Note: deleting a controller also removes all of its **Process Routing** and **Channel Mappings** entries.

---

## The Settings

### Image Staging Root

The folder where OHD puts each job's images. OHD makes a subfolder named after the job, for example `ORD-O4YK5Z-1`, and copies the images into it. The images keep their file names.

OHD copies all the images before it writes the order file, so Frontier never sees an order whose images aren't there yet. OHD doesn't delete the images afterwards.

### Image Path (Fuji JobMaker view)

The same folder as **Image Staging Root**, but written the way the Fuji PC reaches it, for example `\\server\share\Artwork` or a mapped drive letter. This is the path OHD writes into the order file, so if it's wrong the Fuji machine can't find the images.

* Note: if OHD and JobMaker run on the same PC, it's the same path as **Image Staging Root**.
* Note: when you save, OHD warns you if it can't reach this path, but saves anyway. The Fuji PC may see folders the OHD computer can't.
* Note: when a job is sent, OHD checks for the job's folder. If it can see the path but not the folder, the send stops with an error. If it can't see the path at all, it sends anyway, and the first sign of a problem may be the **Failure Timeout** warning.

### Output Path

The JobMaker hot folder: the folder the Fuji software watches for new orders. OHD writes each job's order file here, named after the job and surface, for example `BALLY-Q7F39E-1_Lustre.txt`.

* Note: the folder must already exist. OHD doesn't create it, and the send fails with **Fuji JobMaker hot folder does not exist**.
* Note: this is a different folder from **Image Staging Root**. The order files go in the hot folder; the images go in the staging folder.

### Printer Name (optional)

The Frontier printer to send to, for example **DL650-A1**. Leave it blank to let Frontier choose.

### Auto Correct

* **Default (use printer setting):** Frontier uses whatever the printer is set to.
* **On** or **Off:** turns the printer's automatic image correction on or off for these orders.

### Back Print Mode and Back Print Template

* **None:** nothing is printed on the back.
* **Text:** prints a line on the back of each print, made from the **Back Print Template**, for example `{firstName}/{filename}/{date}`.

You can use these tokens: `{customerName}` `{firstName}` `{lastName}` `{orderNumber}` `{jobName}` `{jobId}` `{filename}` `{originalFilename}` `{date}`. The line can be up to 40 characters, and anything longer is cut off. The characters `%` `(` `;` `'` are replaced with spaces, and `~` with `-`.

* Note: image back prints aren't supported yet.

### Failure Timeout (minutes)

If the Fuji machine hasn't picked up an order after this many minutes, OHD writes a warning to the **Activity Log** so you can check it. It can be 1–1440 minutes; the default is 30.

* Note: the job's status in the Jobs list doesn't change. If an order doesn't appear on the Frontier, check the **Activity Log**.

### Auto Print — Send jobs to print automatically

When ticked, jobs for this controller are sent as soon as they're ready. When unticked, they wait for you to click **Process**. You can also turn this on and off with the **Auto Print** tick box on the controller's card.

### Combine jobs from the same order

When one order has several jobs for this printer (for example 6x4s and 5x7s), OHD sends them to Frontier as one order instead of one per job. Jobs on the same surface go in one order file; jobs on different surfaces go as separate files.

This applies to automatic sending and to **Process**: clicking **Process** on one job sends it together with the order's other jobs that are ready.

**Maximum wait for the rest of the order (minutes):** a safety net only. OHD normally sends the combined order as soon as all its jobs are ready. If one job is held up, OHD stops waiting after this many minutes and sends each ready job as its own Frontier order, not combined. The held-up job stays held. Leave it blank for 30 minutes.

* Note: reprints are always sent on their own.

### Order number prefix rules (optional)

Removes or shortens a fixed tag at the start of order numbers, for example `PXDEMO-`. On Fuji JobMaker, the rules change only the **Order ID** Frontier shows, for example `L-BALLY-Q7F39E-1` becomes `L-Q7F39E-1`. The file name and image folder keep the full job number.

1. Click **+ Add rule**.
2. Type the tag to change.
3. Leave **Replace with** blank to remove the tag, or type a replacement.

* Note: the JobMaker manual allows up to 10 characters in an Order ID, and OHD's are usually longer. If your Frontier cuts them short or refuses them, use these rules to shorten them.

---

## Telling OHD Which Print Code and Surface to Use: Channel Mappings

The controller tells OHD **where** to send a job. **Channel Mappings** tell it **how** to print each product: which Quick Print code and which paper surface.

### How a job finds its controller

1. **Process Routing** (in **Settings → Routing**) sends each process type to a controller. For example, all **Photo Print** jobs go to **Fuji Frontier**.
2. **Channel Mappings** then match the job's product code, and optionally its options, to a print code and surface on that controller.

### Adding a mapping from a job (the easy way)

When a job arrives for a product that has no mapping yet, it shows an **Assign** button in the Jobs list instead of **Process**.

1. Click **Assign**. The **Assign Channel** window opens.
2. In **Print Code**, type the Frontier Quick Print code, exactly as it appears on the Quick Print list, for example **6x4**.
3. In **Print Size**, type the size as width x height, for example **6x4** or **3.5x5**. OHD uses this for cropping in Job Review. It isn't sent to the Frontier, so it doesn't have to match the **Print Code**.
4. In **Surface**, type the Frontier paper surface, for example **Lustre**. It must match exactly, including capital letters.
5. Optional: in **Surface Code**, type a short code for the start of the Order ID, for example **L**. If you leave it blank, OHD uses the first letter of the **Surface**.
6. Optional: tick **Skip Auto Print** if jobs on this channel should always wait for you to click **Process**.
7. Click **Save & Assign**.

Every later job with the same product and options uses this mapping automatically.

![Fuji channel assignment](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/ee18d99e-56cb-4c43-a779-3d57ff03dbf8.png)

### Managing mappings in Settings

In **Settings → Routing → Channel Mappings**, click **+ Add Channel Mapping** to add a mapping, or edit and delete existing ones. The **Add Channel Mapping** window has the same fields, plus **Controller**, **Product Code** and **Options (name : value pairs)**.

* Note: tick **Ignore** on an option to skip it when matching jobs. It applies to every mapping on this controller, so jobs whose value for that option varies still match.

---

## What You'll See

* **In the hot folder:** one order file per job, for example `BALLY-Q7F39E-1_Lustre.txt`. With **Combine jobs from the same order** on, it's one file per surface for the whole order, named after the order, for example `BALLY-Q7F39E_Lustre.txt`.
* **When Frontier takes the order**, the file disappears from the hot folder. A file that stays there means Frontier hasn't taken it; check the Frontier's log.
* **In the Image Staging Root:** one folder per job, holding its images.
* **On the Frontier:** the Order ID is the surface code followed by the job number, for example `L-BALLY-Q7F39E-1`.
* **Reprints** from Job Review go to the same hot folder, with **r1**, **r2** and so on in the name.
* **In OrderHub:** when OHD sends a job, it moves to **In Production** and stays there. Sending a job to the printer doesn't mean the prints are finished, so OHD doesn't complete it. You complete the job in OrderHub as usual.

![Fuji TXT Files](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/1327c05d-1cf6-4969-a561-009df18e619f.png)

---

## Good to Know

* The **Print Code** and **Surface** must match the Frontier's setup exactly. Most "printed on the wrong paper or size" problems are a mapping that doesn't match.
* To use the same settings on a second Frontier, click **Duplicate** on the controller's card, rename it and change the paths. **Duplicate** doesn't copy **Process Routing** or **Channel Mappings**.
* Changes to a controller or mapping apply to the next job sent. Orders already in the hot folder aren't affected.
